rubric.why: Identifies nutrition as the process of obtaining and using food.
rubric.description: Nutrition is the process by which organisms obtain and use food.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining nutrition as obtaining and using food.

rubric.why: Gives a valid purpose for using food.
rubric.description: Food is used for energy, growth, repair or maintenance of the body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating at least one valid purpose of food.

modelAnswer: Nutrition is the process by which organisms obtain food and use it for energy, growth, repair and maintenance of the body.

items.followUp: Write two functions of the stem in plants.

rubric.why: Identifies the root’s role in absorbing water and mineral salts from the soil.
rubric.description: Roots absorb water and mineral salts from the soil.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that roots absorb water or mineral salts.

rubric.why: Gives another valid root function, distinct from absorption.
rubric.description: Roots anchor the plant in the soil and may store food.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that roots anchor the plant or store food.

modelAnswer: Roots absorb water and mineral salts from the soil.
Roots anchor the plant in the soil and may also store food.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a source and a sink in the transport of food in plants.

rubric.why: Identifies a source as a part that produces or releases sugars for transport.
rubric.description: A source produces or releases sugars for transport.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a source produces or releases sugars or food.

rubric.why: Identifies a sink as a part that uses or stores transported food.
rubric.description: A sink uses or stores sugars transported to it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a sink uses or stores sugars or food.

modelAnswer: A source is a plant part, usually a photosynthesizing leaf, that produces or releases sugars for transport.
A sink is a plant part that uses or stores the sugars transported to it.

items.followUp: Describe the difference between tissue-level and organ-level organization.

rubric.why: Defines unicellular organization by the organism’s single cell.
rubric.description: A unicellular organism consists of one cell that performs all life functions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a unicellular organism consists of one cell.

rubric.why: Describes multicellular organization as having many cells, which may be specialized.
rubric.description: A multicellular organism has many cells, often specialized for different functions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it has many cells or specialized cells.

rubric.why: Identifies colonial organization as a group of cells living together.
rubric.description: A colonial organism is a group of similar cells living together.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a colony as a group of cells.

rubric.why: Distinguishes a colony from a fully integrated multicellular organism by noting the cells’ independence.
rubric.description: Colonial cells generally retain considerable independence and may perform life functions individually.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that colonial cells retain independence or can function individually.

modelAnswer: In unicellular organization, an organism consists of a single cell that performs all life functions.
In multicellular organization, an organism consists of many cells, which may be specialized for different functions.
In colonial organization, a group of similar cells lives together in a colony.
The cells of a colony generally retain considerable independence and may perform life functions individually.

items.followUp: Describe the structure and functions of the epidermis and cortex in a plant root.

rubric.why: Names conducting elements that make up xylem.
rubric.description: Xylem includes vessels and tracheids; its conducting elements are generally dead and have thickened walls.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming vessels or tracheids as xylem elements.

rubric.description: Xylem transports water and mineral salts from the roots to the rest of the plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that xylem transports water and mineral salts.

rubric.description: Phloem consists mainly of sieve tubes and companion cells; sieve tubes are living conducting cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming sieve tubes or companion cells as phloem components.

rubric.description: Phloem transports sugars and other organic food substances.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that phloem transports sugars or food.

rubric.why: States the route or direction of phloem transport.
rubric.description: Food moves from sources to sinks and may be transported in either direction through the plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating source-to-sink movement or that phloem transport can occur in both directions.

modelAnswer: Xylem is made up mainly of vessels and tracheids; these conducting elements are generally dead and have thickened walls.
Xylem transports water and mineral salts from the roots to the rest of the plant.
Phloem consists mainly of sieve tubes and companion cells; sieve tubes are living conducting cells.
Phloem transports sugars and other organic food substances from sources to sinks.
Phloem transport may occur in either direction, according to the locations of the sources and sinks.
